questions.question: The Biraja Temple, the Rajarani Temple and the Samaleswari Temple are all located in ________.
questions.questionHtml: The Biraja Temple, the Rajarani Temple and the Samaleswari Temple are all located in ________.
questions.solution:
• The Biraja Temple, the Rajarani Temple and the Samaleswari Temple are all located in Odisha.
  • Biraja Temple - 
    • ​Biraja Temple or Viraja Kshetra is one of the ancient Hindu temples located in the Jajpur district of Odisha, India. 
    • This present temple was built in the 13th century. 
    • It is situated in the Jajpur township which is nearly 125 KM north from Bhubaneswar. 
    • The main idol is Devi Durga who is worshipped by the name Viraja.
  • Rajarani Temple - 
    • ​The temple was built during the later stages of the Somavamsi rule in the 11th century AD. 
    • Today the temple today is devoid of any presiding deity, though there are signs in the architecture of the temple to corroborate that it was a temple dedicated to Lord Shiva.
    • The temple is known as Rajarani Temple, because of the red and yellow sandstone called Rajarania that was used in its construction. 
  • Samaleswari Temple - 
    • The  Samaleswari Temple is situated at Sambalpur, Odisha.
    • The abode of Goddess Samaleswari -the presiding deity of Sambalpur is one of the most revered temples of the state. 
    • Goddess Samaleswari was appropriated as the deity of Sambalpur by the Chouhan King Balaram Dev, who became the King of the region in 1542 AD.
    • Sambalpur region is popularly known as Hirakhanda from ancient times. 
    • According to historians, diamonds were exported to Rome from Sambalpur.

questions.question: ________ is the largest slum in Asia.
questions.questionHtml: ________ is the largest slum in Asia.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Dharavi.

Key Points

  • Dharavi is located in Mumbai, Maharashtra, India.
  • It is considered one of the largest slums in Asia and the world.
  • Dharavi spans over 2.1 square kilometers and is home to approximately 700,000 to 1,000,000 people.
  • Despite its poverty, Dharavi is known for its thriving small-scale industries such as pottery, textiles, and recycling.

Additional Information

  • Slum Definition
    • A slum is a densely populated urban residential area characterized by substandard housing and squalor.
    • Slums often lack basic services such as sanitation, clean water, reliable electricity, and adequate living space.
  • Urbanization and Slums
    • Rapid urbanization often leads to the growth of slums as people migrate to cities in search of better economic opportunities.
    • Due to high demand and limited supply of affordable housing, many people end up living in informal settlements.
  • Economic Activity in Dharavi
    • Dharavi is a hub for numerous small-scale industries, generating an estimated annual turnover of over $1 billion USD.
    • These industries include leather goods, textiles, pottery, and food production, among others.
  • Social and Health Challenges
    • Residents of slums like Dharavi often face significant health challenges due to poor living conditions.
    • Common issues include malnutrition, infectious diseases, and lack of access to healthcare services.

questions.question: The Bhaja Caves are located in ______.
questions.questionHtml: The Bhaja Caves are located in ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

Key Points

  • Bhaja Caves is a group of 22 rock-cut caves that date back to the 2nd century BC.
    • It is located in the Pune.
    • The caves belong to the Hinayana Buddhism sect in Maharashtra.
    • These caves are famous for their indications of the awareness of wooden architecture.

Additional Information

questions.question: Where was Babur buried for the first time in 1530?
questions.questionHtml: Where was Babur buried for the first time in 1530?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Agra.

Key Points

  • In 1530 Babur died at Agra at the age of 47 and was temporarily buried within the Aram Bagh.
  • It is the oldest Mughal Garden in India, originally built by the Mughal Emperor Babur in 1528.
  • Later on, he was buried in Bagh-e Babur Garden in Kabul, Afghanistan by Humayun.

Additional Information

  •  Babur is the founder of the Mughal Empire in India.
  • He was a descendant of Timur (on his father’s side) and Genghis Khan (on his Mother’s side).
  • His original name was Zahiruddin Muhammad.
  • On 21st April 1526, Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi within the First Battle of Panipat and quickly occupied Delhi.
  • On March 16, 1527, Babur defeated Rana Sangha, took on the title of “Ghazi”.
  • On May 6, 1529, Babur met the allied Afghans of Bihar and Bengal and defeated them.

questions.question: In which of the following states are the Son Bhandar Caves located?
questions.questionHtml: In which of the following states are the Son Bhandar Caves located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Bihar.

Key Points

  • The Son Bhandhar Caves are located in Rajgir in the state of Bihar.
  • As per an inscription written in the Gupta language/characters on a rock at the entrance, bhandhar caves were constructed by a Jain muni, meaning named Vairadeva, which makes them structures belonging from 4th century BC.
  • The Son Bhandar caves, also Sonebhandar, are two artificial caves located in Rajgir in the state of Bihar in India.
  • They belonged to the Jains.

Additional Information

  • Some other important caves:
  • Elephanta Caves:
    • Location: Elephanta Islands in Mumbai.
    • Developed between A.D. 600 to 1000.
    • Developed under the patronage of the Rashtrakuta kings.
    • Status: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1987).
    • The caves are carved from solid basalt rock.
    • It is a conglomeration of seven caves, out of which the most important is the Mahesa-murti cave. 
  • Ajanta Caves:
    • Location: The Sahyadri ranges (Western Ghats) near Aurangabad (Maharashtra).
    • They were developed between 200 B.C. to 650 A.D.
      • They are older than Ellora caves.
    • Status: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1983).
    • It comprises about 29 rock-cut Buddhist cave monuments.
      • 25 were used as Viharas while 4 were used as Chaitya.
    • Famous fresco paintings of Ajanta are dying princess, flying apsara and preaching Buddha.
    • Travellers like Fa Hien & Hieun Tsang has mentioned the Ajanta caves in their respective books.
    • The paintings in this cave were generally themed around Buddhism – the life of Buddha and Jataka stories.
  • Ellora Caves:
    • Location: In the Sahyadri range of Maharashtra.
    • Locally known as ‘Verul Leni’.
    • They were developed between the 5th & 11th centuries A.D.
    • Status: UNESCO World Heritage site (1983).
    • It is a group of 34 caves out of which 17 are Brahmanical, 12 are Buddhist & 5 are Jain.
    • Guilds from Vidarbha, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu made these caves.
    • The rock paintings of Ellora were done in two series;
      • 1st series: It is focused on Lord Vishnu & Goddess Laxmi.
      • 2nd series: It is focused on Shaiva, apsaras.
    • It is famous for the largest monolithic excavation in the world- the great Kailasa.

questions.question: Rani - Ki - Vav (the Queen's stepwell) is situated on the banks of which river?
questions.questionHtml: Rani - Ki - Vav (the Queen's stepwell) is situated on the banks of which river?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Saraswati River.

Key Points

  • Rani-ki-Vav, on the banks of the Saraswati River, was initially built as a memorial to a king in the 11th century AD. It is located in Gujarat.
  • It is an exceptional example of a distinctive form of subterranean water architecture of the Indian subcontinent.
  • This stepwell was built by the Solanki dynasty’s queen Udayamati in the 11th century as a memorial to her deceased husband Bhimdev I.
  • Over the years, as the Saraswati river changed its course, the massive structure was flooded and lay buried until its excavation by the Archaeological Survey of India in the late 1980s.
  • Rani-ki-Vav highlights the sanctity of water as it is designed as an inverted temple under the earth’s surface. ​

Additional Information

  •  Ganga River: 
    • The Ganges rises in the southern Great Himalayas on the Indian side of the border with the Tibet Autonomous Region of China.
    • Its five major streams—the Bhagirathi, the Alaknanda, the Mandakini, the Dhauliganga, and the Pindar—all rise in the mountainous region of northern Uttarakhand state.
    • Among them, the two main streams are the Alaknanda (the longer of the two), which rises about 30 miles (50 km) north of the Himalayan peak of Nanda Devi, and the Bhagirathi, which rises about 10,000 feet (3,000 m).  above sea level in a subglacial meltwater cave at the base of a Himalayan glacier known as Gangotri.
    • Gangotri itself is a holy place for Hindu pilgrimage. However, the original source of the Ganges is believed to be Gaumukh, about 13 miles (21 km) southeast of Gangotri.
  • Brahmaputra River: 
    • The source of the Brahmaputra is the Chemayungdung Glacier, which covers the Himalayan slopes about 60 miles (100 km) southeast of Mapam Lake in southwestern Tibet.
    • The Kubi, Angasi, and Chemayungdung are the three major streams that originate there.
    • From its source, the river runs in a generally easterly direction for about 700 miles (1,100 km) between the Great Himalayan Range in the south and the Kailas Range in the north.
    • Throughout its upper course, the river is generally referred to as the Tsangpo ("purifier").
    • It is also known by its Chinese name (Yarlung Zangbo) and other local Tibetan names.
  • Krishna River-
    • Krishna is the second largest peninsular river covering the area of Andhra Pradesh, Telengana, Maharashtra, and Karnataka.
    • It originates at Mahabaleshwar Maharashtra.
    • Right bank Tributaries: the Ghatprabha, the Malprabha, and the Tungabhadra.
    • Left Bank Tributaries: the Bhima, the Musi, and the Munneru.
  • Narmada River-
    • ​The Amarkantak region is where the Narmada River, the Son River, and Johila River (Tributary of Son) emerge.
    • It is a west flowing river. Narmada is also known as the Rewa River.
    • The River flows through Gujarat, Chhattisgarh Madhya Pradesh, and Maharashtra.
    • The tributaries of the Narmada River are Kolar River, Shakkar River, Dudhi River, Tawa River, and Hiran River.
  • Kaveri River-
    • ​Talakaveri or Talacauvery in the Bhramagiri Ranges of Karnataka is considered as the origin place of Kaveri.
    • Kaveri is an east-flowing river.
    • It covers the state of Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. 
    • The important tributaries of Kaveri are Harangi, Hemavati, Kabini, Suvarnavathi and Bhavani.
  • Tapi River-
    • ​It originates from Multai in Betul district of Madhya Pradesh.
    • The river flows through M.P., Maharashtra, and Gujarat.
    • Tapi is a west-flowing river.

questions.question: The Rampurva bull that was part of a Mauryan pillar found in Rampurwa, Bihar is now been placed at __________.
questions.questionHtml: The Rampurva bull that was part of a Mauryan pillar found in Rampurwa, Bihar is now been placed at __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Rashtrapati Bhavan.
Key Points
  • The Rampurva bull is a significant artifact of the Mauryan period, and it was discovered as part of a pillar in Rampurva, Bihar.
  • The bull is made of polished sandstone and is believed to have been created during the reign of Emperor Ashoka.
  • In the present day, the Rampurva bull is housed in the Rashtrapati Bhavan, which is the official residence of the President of India.
  • The Rashtrapati Bhavan is located in New Delhi and was designed by Sir Edwin Lutyens, who was also responsible for designing several other iconic landmarks in the city.
Additional Information
  • Pradhan Mantri Bhavan: This is the official residence of the Prime Minister of India and is located on Lok Kalyan Marg in New Delhi.
  • Sansad: This refers to the Indian Parliament, which is located in the Sansad Bhavan complex in New Delhi.
  • Rajpath: This is a ceremonial boulevard in New Delhi that connects the Rashtrapati Bhavan to India Gate and is often used for parades and processions.

questions.question: In which of the following states is Sri Bhramaramba Mallikarjuna Temple located?
questions.questionHtml: In which of the following states is Sri Bhramaramba Mallikarjuna Temple located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Andhra Pradesh.

Key Points

  • Sri Bhramaramba Mallikarjuna Temple or Srisailam Temple is a Hindu temple dedicated to the deities Shiva and Parvati is located in Andhra Pradesh.
  • This temple is one of the twelve Jyotirlingas of Lord Shiva and one of the eighteen Shakti Peethas of goddess Parvati. 
  • Shiva is worshipped as Mallikarjuna and is represented by the lingam. 

Additional Information

  • The temple architecture in India is not the same everywhere.
  • Basically, there are three styles of temple architecture in India:
  1. Nagara Style (North India)
  2. Dravida Style (South India)
  3. Vasara style (Mix of Nagara and Dravida style)
  • Nagara Style:
  1. Built on a stone platform with steps leading up to it.
  2. Have a tower or Shikhara.
  3. Have Grabhagriha ( A place for the idols of god and goddess).
  4. Examples: Kandariya Mahadeo temple at Khajuraho, Lakshamana temple
  • Dravida Style:
  1. Generally enclosed within a compounded wall.
  2. The entrance gateway is known as Gopuram.
  3. The shape of the Temple tower is known as Vimana (similar to Shikhara in Nagara style).
  4. Large water tanks are common in the temple complex.
  5. Examples: Brahadeeshwara temple, Rajarajeswara temple.
  • Vasara style:
  1. This style of temple architecture is a mix of Nagara and Dravid styles.
  2. Examples: Dodda Basappa Temple, Hoysala Temple

questions.question: In which state is Naharkatiya oil field situated?
questions.questionHtml: In which state is Naharkatiya oil field situated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Assam.

Key Points

  • Naharkatiya is one of the two famous oil fields of Assam.
  • The Naharkatiya field is located at a distance of 32 km southwest of Digboi at the left bank of the Burhi Dibing river.
  • The oil was discovered in 1953 and production started in 1954.
  • Naharkatia is a town and a town area committee in the Dibrugarh district in the Indian state of Assam.
  • It is well known for its petroleum and gas reserves. Earlier, Duliajan, the head office town of Oil India Limited was in its circle.  ​

Additional Information

  • The first oil well was discovered in Assam in Digboi.
  • Crude oil was discovered in Digboi in the late 19th century and the first oil well was dug in 1866.
  • Digboi is known as the Oil City of Assam where the first oil well in Asia was drilled. The Assam Oil Company was established in 1899 to oversee production.
  • In 1901, Digboi Refinery was commissioned supplanting the earlier refinery at Margharita.
  • The Indian Oil Corporation Ltd (IOC) took over the refinery and marketing management of Assam Oil Company Ltd. with effect from 1981 and created a separate division. This division has both refinery and marketing operations.
  • The refinery at Digboi had an installed capacity of 0.50 million tonnes per year.
  • Assam has 4 refineries- Noonmati Refinery, Namuligarh Refinery, Bongaigaon Refinery, and Digboi Refinery.

questions.question: Lakshmibai National Institute of Physical Education (LNIPE) is located at ______.
questions.questionHtml: Lakshmibai National Institute of Physical Education (LNIPE) is located at ______.
questions.solution: Lakshmibai National Institute of Physical Education (LNIPE) is located in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh. Established in 1957 by the Ministry of Education, Government of India, the institute is named after the Indian freedom fighter Rani Lakshmibai and focuses on physical education and sports. LNIPE offers undergraduate, postgraduate, and doctoral programs in these fields, aiming to promote and develop skilled professionals. The institute boasts state-of-the-art facilities and engages in significant research activities. Additionally, LNIPE collaborates with various national and international organizations to enhance sports and physical education globally.

questions.question: For which of the following productions is the Ramagundam power plant famous?
questions.questionHtml: For which of the following productions is the Ramagundam power plant famous?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is thermal energy.

Key Points

  • The Ramagundam power plant is famous for the production of thermal energy.
  • NTPC Ramagundam Thermal Power Plant is located in Telangana.
  • It is part of the National Thermal Power Corporation, a 2600 MW power station located in Ramagundam, Telangana.
  • It is currently the largest power station in South India.
  • It is the first "Super Thermal Power Station" ISO 14001 certified in India.

Additional Information

  • Important thermal plants of India:
    • Hussain Sagar Thermal Power Station:
      • ​It is the historic thermal power plant that was located in Hyderabad, Telangana on the banks of Hussain Sagar.
      • It was India's first thermal power station, opened in 1920 by the erstwhile seventh Nizam of Hyderabad.
    • Mundra Ultra Mega Power Project or Mundra UMPP:
      • It is a sub-bituminous coal-fired power plant in Tundra village at Mundra, Kutch district, Gujarat, India.
      • It is the 3rd largest operational power plant in India.
      • The power plant is owned by Tata Power.
    • The Vindhyachal Thermal Power Station:
      • It is located in the Singrauli district in the Indian state of Madhya Pradesh.

questions.question: In which city of Gujarat will you find the Uparkot Buddhist Caves?
questions.questionHtml: In which city of Gujarat will you find the Uparkot Buddhist Caves?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Junagadh. 

Key Points

  • Uparkot Buddhist Caves are located in Junagadh.
  • Uparkot caves are ancient man-made caverns.
  • The caves are a part of the Junagadh Buddhist Cave Groups.
  • It is situated in the eastern part of Junagadh of Gujarat. 

Additional Information

  • Ajanta is a series of rock-cut caves in the Sahyadri ranges on the Waghora river near Aurangabad in Maharashtra.
    • There are a total of 29 caves(all Buddhist).
    • 25 caves were used as Viharas or residential caves while 4 were used as Chaitya or prayer hills.
  • Kanheri caves are rock-cut caves related to Buddhism located in Sanjay Gandhi National Park, Maharashtra.
    • These caves served as Viharas and Chaityas to the Buddhist monks.
  • Ellora caves is a famous cave located in the Sambhajinagar (former Aurangabad) district of Maharashtra, India.
    • It is one of the UNESCO World Heritage Sites in India.
    • Designated as the UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983.

questions.question: Aga Khan Palace is located in _____ city of Maharashtra.
questions.questionHtml: Aga Khan Palace is located in _____ city of Maharashtra.
questions.solution: The Aga Khan Palace is located in Pune, Maharashtra and was built by Sultan Muhammed Shah Aga Khan III in 1892 as an act of charity to help the poor affected by famine. He was the 48th Imam of the Nizari Ismaili sect and played an important role in giving Muslims a political voice against the British. He was also a founding member and first president of the All India Muslim League in 1906.

questions.question: The beautiful square-shaped Mughal architecture, Kanch Mahal is situated in which of the following cities of India?
questions.questionHtml: The beautiful square-shaped Mughal architecture, Kanch Mahal is situated in which of the following cities of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Agra.

Key Points

  • Kanch Mahal is a beautiful example of Mughal architecture located in Agra, India.
  • It is a square-shaped structure built during the reign of Jahangir in the early 17th century.
  • Originally, Kanch Mahal served as a royal hunting lodge for the Mughal emperors.
  • The building is known for its intricate tile work and splendid architectural design.

Additional Information

  • Mughal Architecture
    • Mughal architecture is a style developed by the Mughals in the 16th, 17th, and 18th centuries throughout the extent of their empire in the Indian subcontinent.
    • It is known for its large-scale use of marble, intricate carvings, and symmetrical designs.
    • Famous examples include the Taj Mahal, Red Fort, and Humayun's Tomb.
    • This architectural style is a blend of Islamic, Persian, Turkish, and Indian architecture.
  • Agra
    • Agra is a city on the banks of the Yamuna river in the Indian state of Uttar Pradesh.
    • It is renowned for its Mughal-era buildings, including the Taj Mahal, Agra Fort, and Fatehpur Sikri.
    • Agra was the capital of the Mughal Empire during the 16th and early 18th centuries.
    • The city is a major tourist destination because of its many splendid Mughal-era buildings.
  • Jahangir
    • Jahangir was the fourth Mughal Emperor who ruled from 1605 to 1627.
    • His reign is characterized by the development of Mughal art and culture.
    • He was known for his interest in art, architecture, and nature.
    • Jahangir's era saw the construction of many significant buildings and gardens.
  • Tile Work
    • Tile work refers to the decorative tiles used in the construction and ornamentation of buildings.
    • It involves the use of glazed and unglazed tiles to create intricate patterns and designs.
    • Tile work was a popular decorative technique in Mughal architecture.
    • The tiles are often brightly colored and feature geometric and floral designs.

questions.question: The town of Paro is a famous tourism destination of ______.
questions.questionHtml: The town of Paro is a famous tourism destination of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Bhutan.

Key Points

  • Paro is a valley town in Bhutan, west of the capital, Thimphu.
  • It is the site of the country’s only international airport and is also known for the many sacred sites in the area. 

Additional Information

  • Recently 17 Iconic Tourist Sites into world-class tourist destinations, to boost the tourism influx in India.
  • The 17 iconic Tourists sites are:
    • Taj Mahal and Fatehpur Sikri (Uttar Pradesh),
    • Ajanta & Ellora (Maharashtra),
    • Humayun’s Tomb, Red Fort and Qutub Minar (Delhi),
    • Colva (Goa),
    • Amer Fort (Rajasthan),
    • Somnath and Dholavira (Gujarat),
    • Khajuraho (Madhya Pradesh),
    • Hampi (Karnataka),
    • Mahabalipuram (Tamil Nadu),
    • Kaziranga (Assam),
    • Kumarakom (Kerala) and
    • The Mahabodhi Temple (Bihar)
  • World Tourism Day is celebrated on 27 September.

questions.question: What is the name of the Centre for the Study of Culture and Civilization in Shimla?
questions.questionHtml: What is the name of the Centre for the Study of Culture and Civilization in Shimla?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Tagore Centre.

  • Tagore Centre is the name of the Centre for the Study of Culture and Civilization in Shimla.

Key Points

  • The Tagore Centre for the Study of Culture and Civilization was inaugurated by the Former President Pranab Mukherjee at the Indian Institute of Advanced Studies (IIAS) in Shimla and also addressed the first Rabindranath Tagore Memorial Lecture.
  • The objectives of the Tagore Centre are:
    • To facilitate the study of Tagore's work.
    • Support interpretations of Tagore's work into other Indian languages.
    • promote comparative study of his work with poets, artists and writers in other parts of India and the world.
    • Explore concerns regarding the relationship between science and society.

Additional Information

  • Nehru Centre is located in Mumbai.
    • The centre facilitates the scientific study of astronomy.

questions.question: The Kyaik Htee Yoe pagoda is located in:
questions.questionHtml: The Kyaik Htee Yoe pagoda is located in:
questions.solution:
The Kyaik Htee Yoe pagoda(It's also known as Golden Rock) is located in Myanmar(Burma).

  • It's a well known Buddhist pilgrimage site in Mon Province. 
  • It is a 24 ft pilgrimage built on the top of a granite boulder covered with gold leaf pasted by its male devotees.
  • Precariously perched on a strand of Buddha's hair. 
  • The rock and the pagoda are situated at the top of Mt. Kyaiktiyo.
  • This is the third-largest Buddhist pilgrimage site in Burma after the Mahamuni Pagoda and Shwedagon Pagoda.

questions.question: Where is Red Lake found?
questions.questionHtml: Where is Red Lake found?
questions.solution: Red Lake, located in the USA, is a significant freshwater body in the state of Minnesota. It's renowned for being one of the largest natural lakes in the United States & is split into two parts, Upper Red Lake & Lower Red Lake, by a narrow peninsula. The lake is a key site for fishing, particularly known for its abundant walleye population. Its importance extends beyond recreation, serving as a vital resource for the local Red Lake Band of Chippewa Indians, both culturally & economically.

questions.question: The Araku Valley, a tourist resort, is located near which of these cities of South India?
questions.questionHtml: The Araku Valley, a tourist resort, is located near which of these cities of South India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Visakhapatnam.

Key Points

  • Araku Valley is a hill station in the Vishakhapatnam district of Andhra Pradesh.
  • This tourist spot is present in the Ananthagiri Hills of Eastern Ghats.
  • It is also inscribed as 'Ooty of Andhra'.
  • The area is also exploited for Bauxite mining.
  • Jindanghada peak, the highest peak of Andhra Pradesh and the Eastern Ghats also rises here.
  • It is also famous for the well-known Borra caves.

questions.question: With which of the following was Kadri Gopalnath associated?
questions.questionHtml: With which of the following was Kadri Gopalnath associated?
questions.solution: Kadri Gopalnath was associated with the Saxophone. He was a pioneer of Carnatic music for the alto saxophone and received numerous honors for his contributions to the field. The sitar is a plucked stringed instrument, the tabla is a small drum, and the flute is a woodwind instrument.

questions.question: In which of the following UT/states is Hemkund Sahib located?
questions.questionHtml: In which of the following UT/states is Hemkund Sahib located?
questions.solution: Hemkund Sahib is located in Uttarakhand, a state in northern India. It is a Sikh place of worship and pilgrimage site devoted to Guru Gobind Singh. It is situated in the Garhwal Himalayas at an elevation of 4,160 meters. Uttarakhand is also home to several national parks, including Corbett National Park, Rajaji National Park, and Nanda Devi National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

questions.question: The famous hill station named Mcleodganj is located in:
questions.questionHtml: The famous hill station named Mcleodganj is located in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Himachal Pradesh.

  • Mcleodganj is a beautiful hill station with breathtaking landscapes near Dharamshala (Kangra district).

Key Points

  • Mcleodganj's culture is a beautiful amalgamation of Tibetan with some British influence.
  • It is also known as Little Lhasa or Dhasa because it comprises a large number of Tibetans.
  • It is famous for its museums, temples, waterfalls, lakes, and monasteries.
  • The sightseeing locations include the residence of Dalai Lama, Bhagsu Falls and Bhagsunath Temple, Namgyal Monastery and Tibetan museum.

questions.question: Amar Jawan Jyoti was installed under the Arch of India Gate in January ______.
questions.questionHtml: Amar Jawan Jyoti was installed under the Arch of India Gate in January ______.
questions.solution: Amar Jawan Jyoti, a memorial for soldiers who died in the Indo-Pakistani War of 1971, was installed under the Arch of India Gate in January 1972. It served as India's national war memorial until February 2019. The older flame was merged with the newer one at the National War Memorial in January 2022 and is now located at the Amar Chakra.
